name: Geshem
overview: Geshem was a male Arab figure known for opposing Nehemiah during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. His identity is primarily noted through his opposition role, with no additional tribal or familial details recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Geshem, also rendered as Gashmu, means 'rain shower' in the biblical text. This proper name appears in Nehemiah 2:19 and Nehemiah 6:6, reflecting the same meaning without indication of divine origin.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Geshem beyond his identification as an Arab opponent of Nehemiah. No further relationships are documented in the biblical narrative.
scriptureSignificance: Geshem's significance lies in his opposition to Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild Jerusalem's walls, representing external resistance to God's work through His servant. His presence in the narrative highlights the challenges faced by God's people in restoring the city and reestablishing worship and security. As an Arab adversary, Geshem embodies the broader opposition from surrounding peoples during this critical period of restoration.
